</table>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS1.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S3.SS1.p9.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="58.92" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 477.38 58.92" width="477.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,58.92) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#4040FF;" fill="#4040FF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 4.15 L 0 54.77 C 0 57.06 1.86 58.92 4.15 58.92 L 473.23 58.92 C 475.52 58.92 477.38 57.06 477.38 54.77 L 477.38 4.15 C 477.38 1.86 475.52 0 473.23 0 L 4.15 0 C 1.86 0 0 1.86 0 4.15 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#F2F2FF;" fill="#F2F2FF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.38 4.15 L 1.38 54.77 C 1.38 56.29 2.62 57.53 4.15 57.53 L 473.23 57.53 C 474.75 57.53 475.99 56.29 475.99 54.77 L 475.99 4.15 C 475.99 2.62 474.75 1.38 473.23 1.38 L 4.15 1.38 C 2.62 1.38 1.38 2.62 1.38 4.15 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 13.62 9.39)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:32.53em;--ltx-fo-height:3.09em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;" height="45.51" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 42.82)" width="450.12"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="S3.SS1.p9.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:32.53em;">
<span id="S3.SS1.p9.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS1.p9.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Observation 1:<span id="S3.SS1.p9.pic1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Existing greedy certainty-based samplers often fail to find near-optimal decoding paths.</span></span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p10.1" class="ltx_p">As illustrated in Figure <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, an optimal decoding action should be evaluated not only by its own prediction certainty but also by the <span id="S3.SS1.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">information gain</span> it provides for the remainder of the generation process. To address the limitations of existing samplers, it is essential to account for this information gain when making current decisions. As shown in Figure <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, our proposed Info-Gain Sampler effectively addresses this one-way challenge by prioritizing the decoding of factors with an 84% probability.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p11" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p11.1" class="ltx_p">In standard ARMs, assessing information gain typically requires computationally expensive techniques, such as Monte Carlo Tree Search, to simulate future trajectories. This is primarily due to the next-token bottleneck: since ARMs only provide the probability of the immediate next token, multi-step look-ahead becomes prohibitively slow.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p12" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S3.SS1.p12.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="58.92" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 477.38 58.92" width="477.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,58.92) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#4040FF;" fill="#4040FF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 4.15 L 0 54.77 C 0 57.06 1.86 58.92 4.15 58.92 L 473.23 58.92 C 475.52 58.92 477.38 57.06 477.38 54.77 L 477.38 4.15 C 477.38 1.86 475.52 0 473.23 0 L 4.15 0 C 1.86 0 0 1.86 0 4.15 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#F2F2FF;" fill="#F2F2FF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.38 4.15 L 1.38 54.77 C 1.38 56.29 2.62 57.53 4.15 57.53 L 473.23 57.53 C 474.75 57.53 475.99 56.29 475.99 54.77 L 475.99 4.15 C 475.99 2.62 474.75 1.38 473.23 1.38 L 4.15 1.38 C 2.62 1.38 1.38 2.62 1.38 4.15 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 13.62 9.39)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:32.53em;--ltx-fo-height:3.09em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;" height="45.51" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 42.82)" width="450.12"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="S3.SS1.p12.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:32.53em;">
<span id="S3.SS1.p12.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS1.p12.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Question 2:<span id="S3.SS1.p12.pic1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Can Masked Diffusion Models efficiently assess information gain of a decoding action?</span></span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p13" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p13.1" class="ltx_p">Unlike ARMs, MDMs don’t have the next-token bottleneck. MDMs leverage bidirectional attention, allowing the model to simultaneously evaluate the impact of any decoding action on the uncertainty of the entire sequence. This architectural advantage enables the model to “see” how filling a mask affects the uncertainty of all remaining masks in a single forward pass.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p14" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S3.SS1.p14.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="75.52" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 477.38 75.52" width="477.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,75.52) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#4040FF;" fill="#4040FF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 4.15 L 0 71.37 C 0 73.66 1.86 75.52 4.15 75.52 L 473.23 75.52 C 475.52 75.52 477.38 73.66 477.38 71.37 L 477.38 4.15 C 477.38 1.86 475.52 0 473.23 0 L 4.15 0 C 1.86 0 0 1.86 0 4.15 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#F2F2FF;" fill="#F2F2FF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.38 4.15 L 1.38 71.37 C 1.38 72.9 2.62 74.14 4.15 74.14 L 473.23 74.14 C 474.75 74.14 475.99 72.9 475.99 71.37 L 475.99 4.15 C 475.99 2.62 474.75 1.38 473.23 1.38 L 4.15 1.38 C 2.62 1.38 1.38 2.62 1.38 4.15 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 13.62 9.39)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:32.53em;--ltx-fo-height:4.29em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;" height="62.11" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 59.42)" width="450.12"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="S3.SS1.p14.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:32.53em;">
<span id="S3.SS1.p14.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS1.p14.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Observation 2:<span id="S3.SS1.p14.pic1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> MDMs’ bidirectional architecture enables efficient information gain estimation in one forward pass, bypassing expensive iterative computations.</span></span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Information Gain Sampler</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The insights from <span id="S3.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Observation 1</span> and <span id="S3.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Observation 2</span> suggest that greedy optimization alone is insufficient for minimizing cumulative uncertainty across the entire sequence.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce the <span id="S3.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Information Gain (Info-Gain) Sampler</span> which leverages the bidirectional nature of MDMs to balance the immediate uncertainty cost of a decoding decision against its expected information gain over the remaining masked positions.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.2.1 </span>Objective of Info-Gain Sampler</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We first define <span id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">state uncertainty</span> as the average marginal entropy over the masked positions in state <math id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}(z_{t})=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{M}_{t}|}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{M}_{t}}H^{(\ell)}(z_{t})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></munder><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}(z_{t})=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{M}_{t}|}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{M}_{t}}H^{(\ell)}(z_{t})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The state uncertainty quantifies the information remaining to be resolved by the model and can be computed efficiently via a single forward pass.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The <span id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">information gain</span> of action <math id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is defined as the reduction in state uncertainty (equivalently, the decrease in marginal entropy over the remaining masked positions) it induces:</p>
<table id="S3.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{IG}(a_{t};z_{t}):=\mathcal{H}(z_{t})-\mathcal{H}(z_{t-1})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>IG</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{IG}(a_{t};z_{t}):=\mathcal{H}(z_{t})-\mathcal{H}(z_{t-1})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t-1}=\text{Apply}(z_{t},a_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>Apply</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t-1}=\text{Apply}(z_{t},a_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the state obtained after executing action <math id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> from state <math id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The total impact of a decoding action <math id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is thus decomposed into two components:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(1) Immediate Cost:</span> the uncertainty of the tokens being decoded in the current step, measured by the sum of marginal entropy over the chosen positions <math id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C(a_{t}\mid z_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C(a_{t}\mid z_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(2) Information Gain:</span> the reduction in the uncertainty over the remaining mask positions, quantified by the information gain <math id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{IG}(a_{t};z_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>IG</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{IG}(a_{t};z_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">To balance these two components, we define the Info-Gain Sampler objective as:</p>
<table id="S3.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{IG}(a_{t}\mid z_{t})=\underbrace{\text{IG}(a_{t};z_{t})}_{\text{Information Gain}}-\underbrace{C(a_{t}\mid z_{t})}_{\text{Immediate Cost}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mtext>IG</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>Information Gain</mtext></munder><mo>−</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>Immediate Cost</mtext></munder></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{IG}(a_{t}\mid z_{t})=\underbrace{\text{IG}(a_{t};z_{t})}_{\text{Information Gain}}-\underbrace{C(a_{t}\mid z_{t})}_{\text{Immediate Cost}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">We provide further theoretical analysis in Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Theoretical Analysis of the Info-Gain Objective ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.2.2 </span>Implementation of Info-Gain Sampler</h4>

<figure id="S3.F2" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18176v1/workflow_v2.png" id="S3.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/271;" width="476" height="271" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="S3.F2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">The Info-Gain Sampler workflow. Starting from state <math id="S3.F2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{T_{0}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{T_{0}}</annotation></semantics></math>, the sampler iteratively: (1) samples candidate actions, (2) evaluates <math id="S3.F2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{\text{IG}}=\text{Immediate Cost}-\text{Information Gain}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mtext>IG</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>Immediate Cost</mtext><mo>−</mo><mtext>Information Gain</mtext></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{\text{IG}}=\text{Immediate Cost}-\text{Information Gain}</annotation></semantics></math> in parallel to select the optimal successor state <math id="S3.F2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t-1}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t-1}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>, and (3) executes the state transition until reaching the final sequence <math id="S3.F2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Action Sampler.</span> Following previous work <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Peng et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, we explore the large action space by generating a candidate set <math id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math> of size <math id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> through a two-stage sampling process: (1) <span id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Token Sampling</span>: drawing tokens <math id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> with token temperature <math id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{token}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>token</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{token}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and (2) <span id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Position Sampling</span>: selecting positions <math id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell\in\mathcal{M}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell\in\mathcal{M}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> using a softmax over certainty scores <math id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi(\ell,z_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi(\ell,z_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> with position temperature <math id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{pos}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>pos</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{pos}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Each candidate action <math id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{t}=\{(\ell,v_{\ell})\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t}=\{(\ell,v_{\ell})\}</annotation></semantics></math> is formed by pairing these samples, providing a diverse and high-quality set for evaluation. The size of <math id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is determined by a step scheduling function.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">At each decoding step, Info-Gain Sampler follows a three-step cycle to determine and execute the most informative action (Figure <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3.2.2 Implementation of Info-Gain Sampler ‣ 3.2 Information Gain Sampler ‣ 3 Method ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>):</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(1) Sampling:</span> We sample a candidate set <math id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}=\{a_{t}^{(1)},\dots,a_{t}^{(N)}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}=\{a_{t}^{(1)},\dots,a_{t}^{(N)}\}</annotation></semantics></math> of diverse actions using the <span id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Action Sampler</span>. This step explores the combinatorially large action space by proposing multiple potential actions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(2) Evaluation:</span> We compute the objective <math id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J(a_{t}\mid z_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(a_{t}\mid z_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> for all candidates <math id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> in the set <math id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math>. Crucially, as noted in the previous section, this evaluation is highly efficient as it requires only a single batched forward pass to estimate the future information gain for all candidates simultaneously.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(3) Transition:</span> The optimal action is selected as <math id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{t}^{*}=\arg\max_{a\in\mathcal{C}}J_{IG}(a\mid z_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>J</mi><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t}^{*}=\arg\max_{a\in\mathcal{C}}J_{IG}(a\mid z_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>. We then execute this action to transition to the next state <math id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t-1}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t-1}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>, repeating the cycle until all masked positions are filled and a complete sequence is generated.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.2.3 </span>Efficient Implementation of Info-Gain Sampler</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To ensure efficiency, candidate evaluations are performed in parallel within a single batched forward pass. We further optimize the sampler by restricting the information-gain computation to the current active block <math id="S3.SS2.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Arriola et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, which enables effective KV caching. Additionally, we implement a high-confidence bypass: if the maximum token probability exceeds a threshold <math id="S3.SS2.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>, the corresponding positions are directly fixed into the action set. If the number of such high-confidence positions exceeds the predefined size of the action set for the current step, only the top-<math id="S3.SS2.SSS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> positions with the highest confidence are selected for decoding. This hybrid approach, inspired by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al. (2025b)</a></cite>, significantly reduces inference latency while preserving planning quality. Because Info-Gain effectively reduces uncertainty during decoding, the high-confidence bypass is triggered more frequently, making the mechanism exceptionally efficient.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.2.4 </span>Why is Info-Gain effective</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">State uncertainty</span> serves as an effective indicator for determining whether the current decoding state lies close to the <span id="S3.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">training data manifold</span>. When the decoded content is logically coherent and fluently expressed, the state resides near the data manifold, resulting in a concentrated predictive probability distribution and low uncertainty. Conversely, if the model lacks sufficient training on certain text forms, once decoding enters such inadequately covered regions during inference, it exhibits characteristics of a dispersed probability distribution and high uncertainty. Since the training data distribution represents logically sound and semantically coherent text forms, high uncertainty suggests that the current state may have deviated from the data manifold, indicating potential logical errors or peculiar expressions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.SSS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Existing greedy certainty-based samplers share a fundamental limitation: they cannot recognize the data manifold deviation signals reflected by state uncertainty. These methods select the most certain action at each step, but locally certain actions do not necessarily correspond to actions that keep subsequent states on the data manifold. Local confidence cannot effectively determine whether an action will lead to future deviations. In contrast, the Info-Gain Sampler actively perceives and utilizes state uncertainty through its information-gain term. When a candidate action would cause the state to deviate from the data manifold, the resulting state exhibits increased uncertainty, which negatively impacts the information-gain term and prevents such actions from being prioritized. This mechanism of identifying and maintaining the data manifold through state uncertainty perception enables the Info-Gain Sampler to preserve logical coherence and fluent expression throughout the decoding path, even under high sampling temperatures.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.T2" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S3.T2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 2</span>: </span><span id="S3.T2.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Performance on the full-attention MDM (<span id="S3.T2.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dream-7B</span>). <section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Experiments</h2>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Experimental Setup</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Benchmarks.</span>
We evaluate the effectiveness of the Info-Gain Sampler on diverse settings:
(1) Fully-Attention MDM Reasoning:
Math (GSM8K, MATH-500; 0-shot) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cobbe et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hendrycks et al., 2021</a>)</cite>,
Code (HumanEval, MBPP; 0-shot) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Austin et al., 2021b</a>)</cite>,
and Planning (4<math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>4 Sudoku; 5-shot <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qin et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, Countdown; 3-shot with 3 numbers <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ye et al., 2025</a>)</cite>),
reporting average Pass@1 accuracy over 5 runs;
(2) Semi-Autoregressive MDM Reasoning:
evaluated on the same Math and Code benchmarks
in a zero-shot setting, reporting average Pass@1 accuracy over 5 runs;
(3) Multimodal Text-to-Image Generation:
evaluated on ImageNet-512 and GenEval <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ghosh et al., 2023</a>)</cite>,
with IS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Salimans et al., 2016</a>)</cite>, FID <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Heusel et al., 2017</a>)</cite>,
and sFID <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Radford et al., 2018</a>; <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Salimans et al., 2016</a>)</cite> reported for ImageNet-512,
and attribute-wise scores for GenEval;
(4) Creative Writing:
evaluated on AlpacaEval <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, using an LLM-as-a-judge to compute
the length-controlled win rate <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dubois et al., 2024</a>)</cite> against baselines following past works <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nguyen et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Models.</span> For reasoning tasks, we use Dream-7B-Instruct <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ye et al., 2025</a>)</cite> as the fully-attention representative, and SDAR-8B-Chat <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cheng et al., 2025</a>)</cite> and TraDo-8B-Instruct <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025</a>)</cite> for block diffusion settings using KV-cache following  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>. For image generation, we employ the MMaDa <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2025</a>)</cite> model.
For Creative Writing, We employ the SDAR-8B-Chat model.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S4.T3.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 3</span>: </span><span id="S4.T3.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Performance on semi-autoregressive MDMs (<span id="S4.T3.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">SDAR-8B-Chat</span> and <span id="S4.T3.6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">TraDo-8B-Instruct</span>). Results are reported under block-wise of 16 with token temperature <math id="S4.T3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{token}}=0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>token</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{token}}=0.7</annotation></semantics></math>. We report the accuracy for each task, along with the average accuracy (Avg.) and cumulative entropy (<math id="S4.T3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo mathsize="1.110em">~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{H}</annotation></semantics></math>) per generation. The Info-Gain Sampler consistently achieves the strongest performance across all settings.</span></figcaption>
<div id="S4.T3.7" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_center ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:345.0pt;height:72.2pt;vertical-align:-34.9pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(-177.4pt,37.1pt) scale(0.492981217763417,0.492981217763417) ;">

<td id="S4.T4.7.1.7.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S4.T4.7.1.7.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">25.0</span></td>
<td id="S4.T4.7.1.7.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S4.T4.7.1.7.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">32.0</span></td>
<td id="S4.T4.7.1.7.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S4.T4.7.1.7.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">58.2</span></td>
<td id="S4.T4.7.1.7.9" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S4.T4.7.1.7.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">63.0</span></td>

<td id="S4.T4.7.1.7.11" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S4.T4.7.1.7.11.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">83.7</span></td></tr>
</table>
</span></div>
</figure>

</figure>
<div id="S4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Baselines.</span>
We compare Info-Gain Sampler against several sampling baselines, including :<span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Uniform</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nie et al., 2025</a>)</cite>,<span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">entropy</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ye et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, <span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">confidence</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chang et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, <span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">margin</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>,<span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">KLASS</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025b</a>)</cite> and <span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">PC-Sampler</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Detailed descriptions of these baselines are provided in Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Formal Definitions of Baseline Samplers ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>.
For Math and code tasks, we adopted a block diffusion approach, as previous studies <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Arriola et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2025b</a>)</cite> have shown that this can significantly improve performance. For planning-centric tasks, we remove positional decoding constraints by setting the block size equal to the total generation length, allowing for global optimization across the entire sequence.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Hyperparameters.</span> For reasoning tasks, we employ a position temperature <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{pos}}=0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>pos</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{pos}}=0.1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=8</annotation></semantics></math> candidates for the Info-Gain Sampler, with the acceleration threshold <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> set to <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.8</annotation></semantics></math>. We evaluate the performance under both <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=2</annotation></semantics></math> tokens per step settings. For text-to-image experiments, we set <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{pos}}=0.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>pos</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{pos}}=0.4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=8</annotation></semantics></math> with a 50-step cosine scheduler. Detailed settings for all benchmarks and baseline-specific parameters are provided in Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Detailed Hyperparameter Settings ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Results and Analysis</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reasoning on Full-Attention MDMs.</span>
As shown in Table <a href="#S3.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 3.2.4 Why is Info-Gain effective ‣ 3.2 Information Gain Sampler ‣ 3 Method ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, Info-Gain Sampler consistently outperforms all baselines on Dream-7B-Instruct with only a marginal increase in generation time (+ 24%) and GPU memory usage (+ 20%) via effective acceleration techniques introduced in Section <a href="#S3.SS2.SSS3" title="3.2.3 Efficient Implementation of Info-Gain Sampler ‣ 3.2 Information Gain Sampler ‣ 3 Method ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2.3</span></a>. Detailed computational overhead analysis is provided in the Appendix. Specifically, Info-Gain Sampler achieves a substantial improvement in average accuracy, outperforming the best-performing baselines by 3.6% when <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=2</annotation></semantics></math> and 2.9% when <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=1</annotation></semantics></math>. Experimental results also show that Info-Gain Sampler achieves a significantly lower cumulative entropy <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{H}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is only 47.8% (<math id="S4.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=2</annotation></semantics></math>) and 50.8% (<math id="S4.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=1</annotation></semantics></math>) of the best-performing baseline, confirming its ability to find more globally optimized trajectories.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reasoning on Semi-AR MDMs.</span>
Results for Semi-AR models (Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>) further validate the robustness of Info-Gain Sampler. Notably, while introducing a non-zero token temperature (<math id="S4.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{token}}=0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>token</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{token}}=0.7</annotation></semantics></math>) degrades the performance of baselines, Info-Gain Sampler maintains a substantial lead, outperforming the best baseline by over 20.3% and 20.8% in average accuracy under <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=1</annotation></semantics></math> settings for SDAR-8B-Chat and TraDo-8B-Instruct, respectively. The consistent reduction in <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{H}</annotation></semantics></math> (e.g., from 210.3 to 74.1 for SDAR-8B-Chat at <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=2</annotation></semantics></math>) across different architectures underscores the universal effectiveness of our information-gain-based objective.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Text-to-Image Generation.</span>
In multimodal settings (Table <a href="#S4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 4.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>), Info-Gain Sampler excels in both alignment and fidelity. It achieves the highest average GenEval score (58.2 vs. 56.3 for Margin) and significantly improves ”positional” (25.0 vs. 19.0) and ”attribute” (32.0 vs. 29.0) sub-scores. Furthermore, on ImageNet-512, Info-Gain Sampler substantially improves FID (from 43.3 to 38.1) and IS (from 53.3 to 63.0), demonstrating its broad generalizability on multimodal generation tasks.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Creative Writing.</span>
For creative writing (Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 4.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>), the Info-Gain Sampler consistently outperforms all baselines across various token temperatures <math id="S4.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{token}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>token</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{token}}</annotation></semantics></math>. At a high temperature of <math id="S4.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{token}}=1.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>token</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{token}}=1.5</annotation></semantics></math>, where increased stochasticity often degrades coherence, our sampler achieves a peak win-rate of <span id="S4.SS2.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">80.3%</span> against the Entropy baseline. By prioritizing informative actions through its lookahead mechanism, the Info-Gain Sampler exhibits superior robustness to temperature scaling in MDMs, effectively balancing creativity and coherence. Across all settings and baselines, it maintains an average win-rate of <span id="S4.SS2.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">63.1%</span>, demonstrating that introducing information gain enhances both creative diversity and textual coherence under temperature variations.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F3" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">

</figure>
<figure id="S4.F4" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18176v1/abla-2.png" id="S4.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:381/379;" width="381" height="379" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F4.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 4</span>: </span><span id="S4.F4.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Impact of different beam sizes on the MATH-500 dataset. Specifically: <span id="S4.F4.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Beam Size = 1</span> is a special case equivalent to the Info-Gain Sampler; <span id="S4.F4.7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Beam Size = Expansion Budget</span> is equivalent to the Best-of-<math id="S4.F4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> (BoN) baseline; and <span id="S4.F4.7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Intermediate Values</span> represent a look-ahead beam search algorithm using Info-Gain as the pruning heuristic.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S4.F5" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18176v1/entropy-vs-temperature.png" id="S4.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/456;" width="476" height="456" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F5.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>: </span><span id="S4.F5.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Temperature Sensitivity.<span id="S4.F5.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Cumulative trajectory uncertainty under varying position and token temperatures on the 100 simple arithmetic problems, evaluated using global decoding with a fixed length of 64 tokens.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Ablation Study</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Optimization of Cumulative Uncertainty.</span>
As shown in Table <a href="#S3.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 3.2.4 Why is Info-Gain effective ‣ 3.2 Information Gain Sampler ‣ 3 Method ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, the <span id="S4.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Info-Gain Sampler</span> significantly outperforms baselines in optimizing cumulative uncertainty. By tracking cumulative entropy during decoding on mathematical reasoning tasks (Fig. <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 4.2 Results and Analysis ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>), we observe that:
(1) The Info-Gain heuristic balances immediate cost with future gains, yielding non-linear entropy growth that stabilizes earlier than the greedy Entropy baseline.
(2) Cumulative entropy shows a strong <span id="S4.SS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">negative correlation with accuracy</span> (Pearson’s <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=-0.70" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.70</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=-0.70</annotation></semantics></math>), validating it as a reliable proxy for decoding quality.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comparison of Info-Gain Variants.</span>
We compare the <span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Info-Gain Sampler</span> (<math id="S4.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B=1</annotation></semantics></math>), <span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Info-Gain Beam Search</span> (<math id="S4.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B&gt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B&gt;1</annotation></semantics></math>), and <span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Best-of-N (BoN)</span> under a fixed computational budget (Figure <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 4.2 Results and Analysis ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>). For beam search variants, we adopt the following configuration: the beam width is set to <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>, and the scoring function is defined as the sum of cumulative entropy and state uncertainty. The decoding process terminates when all hypotheses in the beam have been fully decoded.
(1) The <span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Info-Gain Sampler (<math id="S4.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B=1</annotation></semantics></math>)</span> performs near the Pareto frontier, achieving near-optimal results while remaining highly parallelizable and avoiding complex KV-cache management.
(2) Both Info-Gain variants significantly outperform <span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">BoN</span>, proving that global planning via information gain is superior to simply increasing independent samples.
(3) Increasing <span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Beam Size</span> under given expansion budget yields marginal uncertainty reduction but incurs higher memory overhead (Appendix <a href="#A6.SS1" title="F.1 Memory Overhead Analysis ‣ Appendix F Resource Overhead Analysis ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.1</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Compatibility with Temperature Sampling.</span>
We investigate the impact of position and token temperature settings on cumulative uncertainty. For the baselines, the position temperature mechanism is implemented by applying a softmax with temperature to the heuristic scores followed by categorical sampling, where a position temperature of zero corresponds to the original greedy sampling.
As shown in Figure <a href="#S4.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 4.2 Results and Analysis ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, the Info-Gain Sampler maintains stable, low trajectory uncertainty across various temperature scales without sensitive tuning. Importantly, low cumulative entropy reflects more optimized decoding rather than mode collapse, as evidenced by the preserved diversity and competitive win rates in creative writing (Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 4.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>). In contrast, other baselines are highly sensitive to temperature changes, leading to decoding instability.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Limitation and Future Work</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While the Info-Gain Sampler demonstrates significant improvements in generation quality across multiple domains, there are several avenues for further refinement.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">More Efficient Implementation.</span> Although the Info-Gain Sampler leverages parallel evaluation and acceleration techniques to minimize latency, the search process still incurs higher computational cost than greedy decoding. Future work could explore more efficient lookahead mechanisms, adaptive branching, and hardware-level optimizations to further enhance inference throughput.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Refinement of Action Sampler.</span> Our action sampler currently leverages local uncertainty as a heuristic for candidate generation. Although this approach is robust and yields high-quality plans, future research could investigate more sophisticated sampling strategies that go beyond local heuristics. Such advancements would likely enhance both the diversity and quality of the candidate set.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T6" class="ltx_table">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T6.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 6</span>: </span><span id="S5.T6.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Unified view of MDM samplers. <span id="S5.T6.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Selection Criteria</span> denotes the objective function optimized at each decoding step. <span id="S5.T6.7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Temperature Sensitivity</span> indicates robustness of performance to temperature-based stochastic sampling, while <span id="S5.T6.7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Greedy Location Selection</span> marks whether the sampler selects positions based solely on immediate certainty without considering future information gain.</span></figcaption><div class="ltx_flex_figure">

</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Related Work</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Masked Diffusion Models.</span> Discrete diffusion models provide a non-autoregressive alternative for sequence generation, grounded in theoretical frameworks for discrete and masked data <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Austin et al., 2021a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lou et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rombach et al., 2022</a>)</cite>. Unlike ARMs, which often require training interventions for long-horizon planning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Teoh et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, bidirectionality in MDMs naturally enables global reasoning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ye et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. MDM research has diverged into training large models from scratch, like LLaDA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nie et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, and adapting pre-trained autoregressive models, such as Dream, DiffuLLaMA, and DIMPLE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ye et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gong et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu and others, 2025</a>)</cite>. To enhance long-sequence modeling, hybrid semi-autoregressive (Semi-AR) architectures like Block Diffusion <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Arriola et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, Diffusion Forcing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, and absorbing diffusion variants <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2025</a>)</cite> enable KV-caching for better efficiency. Recent optimizations like Fast-dLLM/v2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2025b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2025a</a>)</cite> and models such as SDAR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cheng et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, TraDo <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, and WeDLM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2025</a>)</cite> have further advanced complex reasoning and long-text generation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Samplers.</span>
Due to the causal factorization, sampling strategies for ARMs typically rely on assessing and regulating local uncertainty in next-token prediction to improve generation quality and diversity. A broad class of samplers has been proposed, including deterministic decoding strategies such as beam search <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2016</a>; <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Freitag and Al-Onaizan, 2017</a>)</cite> and stochastic decoding strategies <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Holtzman et al., 2019</a>; <a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fan et al., 2018</a>; <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nguyen et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.
In contrast to ARMs, Masked Diffusion Models (MDMs) introduce a fundamentally different sampling problem: beyond deciding <em id="S6.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">what</em> token to decode, samplers must also decide <em id="S6.p2.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">where</em> (i.e., which position) to decode within the non-causal sequence. This expanded decision space amplifies the impact of early decoding choices and renders local uncertainty criteria insufficient. Still, existing MDM samplers typically rely on greedy, certainty-based heuristics to select decoding positions, using metrics such as entropy and margin scores <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nie et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ye et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chang et al., 2022</a>)</cite>. Some approaches further incorporate calibration or stability refinements to improve robustness <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">BenHamu et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Nevertheless, these approaches share a common limitation: decoding decisions are made myopically based on greedy metrics. They do not account for the downstream impact of each decoding decision on global uncertainty or information gain across the remaining masked tokens. We provide a comparison between existing samplers for MDMs in Table <a href="#S5.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ 5 Limitation and Future Work ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We propose the <span id="S7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Info-Gain Sampler</span>, a training-free decoding framework for Masked Diffusion Models that exploits bidirectional attention to incorporate information gain in action selection, balancing immediate certainty with future uncertainty reduction and mitigating the myopia of uncertainty-based samplers. Across reasoning, code generation, planning, and image generation tasks, Info-Gain Sampler consistently improves performance, achieving a 3.6% average accuracy gain on 6 reasoning benchmarks under full attention MDM, a 63.1% average win-rate in creative writing, and a 1.9% improvement on GenEval, outperforming prior SOTA baselines and raising the performance ceiling of MDM generation. It remains compatible with both full-attention and semi-autoregressive architectures, reducing <span id="S7.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">cumulative uncertainty</span> and offers a principled bridge from local heuristics to global planning for non-autoregressive generation.</p>
</div>
</section>

<li id="bib.bib24" class="ltx_bibitem ltx_bib_inproceedings"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_bib_author-year ltx_role_refnum ltx_tag_bibitem">Gong <span class="ltx_text ltx_bib_etal">et al.</span> (2025)</span>
<span class="ltx_bibblock"><span class="ltx_text ltx_bib_author">S. Gong, S. Agarwal, Y. Zhang, J. Ye, L. Zheng, M. Li, C. An, P. Zhao, W. Bi, J. Han, <span class="ltx_text ltx_bib_etal">et al.</span></span>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Formal Definitions of Baseline Samplers</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To provide a rigorous comparison, we formalize the action selection mechanism for each baseline sampler. At each decoding step <math id="A1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="A1.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid z_{t},\ell)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid z_{t},\ell)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the predicted token distribution at masked position <math id="A1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell\in\mathcal{M}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell\in\mathcal{M}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. The samplers differ in their scoring function <math id="A1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi(z_{t},\ell)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi(z_{t},\ell)</annotation></semantics></math>, where the top-<math id="A1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> positions with the lowest scores are selected for decoding.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Uniform <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nie et al., 2025</a>)</cite></h5>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This baseline selects positions uniformly at random from the mask set <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A1.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{\text{Uniform}}(z_{t},\ell)=\epsilon,\quad\epsilon\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mtext>Uniform</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{\text{Uniform}}(z_{t},\ell)=\epsilon,\quad\epsilon\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>

</div>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This baseline prioritizes positions where the model is most certain about the top-1 prediction:</p>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
