</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Margin <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025a</a>)</cite></h5>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This baseline considers the gap between the two most likely tokens, selecting positions with the largest margin:</p>
<table id="A1.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{\text{Margin}}(z_{t},\ell)=p_{\text{top1}}-p_{\text{top2}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mtext>Margin</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mtext>top1</mtext></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mtext>top2</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{\text{Margin}}(z_{t},\ell)=p_{\text{top1}}-p_{\text{top2}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">KLASS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025b</a>)</cite></h5>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This method incorporates a KL-divergence constraint to maintain consistency between consecutive decoding steps. Originally, KLASS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025b</a>)</cite> supports dynamic decoding by selecting all positions that satisfy the KL threshold. To ensure a fair performance comparison with other samplers, we adapt it to decode a fixed number of tokens per step. Following the original implementation, we set the threshold <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon=5\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon=5\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>. Effectively, KLASS prioritizes positions where the KL divergence is below the threshold, ranking them by confidence, and only falls back to other positions if more tokens are required. This can be formalized as the following scoring function:</p>
<table id="A1.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E10.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\phi_{\text{Conf}}(z_{t},\ell)+\textbf{1}_{(D_{KL}(p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid z_{t},\ell)\|p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid z_{t+1},\ell))&lt;\epsilon)}\\
" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mtext>Conf</mtext></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">1</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>D</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>z</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>z</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{\text{Conf}}(z_{t},\ell)+\textbf{1}_{(D_{KL}(p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid z_{t},\ell)\|p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid z_{t+1},\ell))&lt;\epsilon)}\\
</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where positions with higher scores are prioritized. In our experiments, we first select positions satisfying the KL constraint based on confidence, and then fill the remaining budget from the other positions.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">PC-Sampler <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang et al., 2025</a>)</cite></h5>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This sampler regulates the decoding trajectory by combining a position-aware weight with content-aware confidence calibration. It modulates the selection priority of each candidate token <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> at position <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> using an exponential decay function <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="w_{\ell}=e^{-\lambda\cdot\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>e</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\ell}=e^{-\lambda\cdot\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math> controls the positional penalty. To discourage generic tokens, it calibrates the confidence score using the token frequency distribution <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\mathcal{D}^{\prime}}(x_{\ell})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\mathcal{D}^{\prime}}(x_{\ell})</annotation></semantics></math> and a content-aware calibration term <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}^{(\ell)}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}^{(\ell)}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A1.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{\text{PC}}(z_{t},\ell)=\mathcal{C}^{(\ell)}_{t}\cdot w_{\ell}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mtext>PC</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{\text{PC}}(z_{t},\ell)=\mathcal{C}^{(\ell)}_{t}\cdot w_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px7" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Block Diffusion <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Arriola et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2025b</a>)</cite></h5>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This sampler employs a position scheduling function <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{t}(\ell)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{t}(\ell)</annotation></semantics></math> that indicates whether position <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> lies within the currently active diffusion block at time step <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>. Specifically, <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{t}(\ell)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{t}(\ell)</annotation></semantics></math> takes the value 1 if <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell\in\mathcal{B}_{\sigma(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell\in\mathcal{B}_{\sigma(t)}</annotation></semantics></math> and 0 otherwise, where <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}_{\sigma(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}_{\sigma(t)}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the active block determined by a scheduling rule <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(t)</annotation></semantics></math>. The sampling process restricts candidate positions to the active block and applies a standard heuristic:</p>
<table id="A1.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{\text{Block}}(z_{t},\ell)=\begin{cases}\phi(z_{t},\ell),&amp;\text{if }I_{t}(\ell)=1,\\
-\infty,&amp;\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mtext>Block</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mtext>if </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext>otherwise</mtext><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{\text{Block}}(z_{t},\ell)=\begin{cases}\phi(z_{t},\ell),&amp;\text{if }I_{t}(\ell)=1,\\
-\infty,&amp;\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Here, the active block <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}_{\sigma(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}_{\sigma(t)}</annotation></semantics></math> slides over time according to <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(t)</annotation></semantics></math>, typically following a sequential or random traversal of the position indices, thereby gradually diffusing information across the entire sequence.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Detailed Hyperparameter Settings</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we provide a detailed overview of the hyperparameter settings used across all experiments. All experiments were conducted on NVIDIA A800 GPUs.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reasoning and Coding Tasks.</span> For tasks involving logical reasoning (GSM8K, MATH500) and code generation (HumanEval, MBPP), we set the token sampling temperature <math id="A2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{token}}=0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>token</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{token}}=0.7</annotation></semantics></math> to strike a balance between output diversity and structural coherence. For the Info-Gain Sampler, we employ a relatively low position temperature <math id="A2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{pos}}=0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>pos</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{pos}}=0.1</annotation></semantics></math> to focus the selection on the most informative candidate positions, while generating <math id="A2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=8</annotation></semantics></math> candidate actions per step for parallel evaluation. To maintain high throughput during predictable decoding phases, we set the acceleration threshold <math id="A2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=0.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma=0.8</annotation></semantics></math>, which allows the sampler to skip the full evaluation routine when the maximum token probability is high. For block diffusion settings on Semi-AR models (SDAR and TraDo), we use a fixed block size of 16. The decoding budget <math id="A2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> (tokens per step) is varied between 1 and 2 to evaluate performance under different acceleration ratios. Maximum generation lengths are benchmark-specific: 256 tokens for GSM8K, HumanEval, and MBPP; 512 tokens for MATH500 and SDAR benchmarks; and 1024 tokens for the TraDo-8B model to accommodate longer reasoning chains.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Text-to-Image Generation.</span> For multimodal experiments using the MMaDa model on ImageNet and GenEval, we adopt a more conservative token temperature <math id="A2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{token}}=0.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>token</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{token}}=0.4</annotation></semantics></math> and a matching position temperature <math id="A2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{pos}}=0.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>pos</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{pos}}=0.4</annotation></semantics></math> to ensure high fidelity and alignment with text prompts. The candidate set size is kept at <math id="A2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=8</annotation></semantics></math>. We follow a 50-step decoding trajectory governed by a cosine schedule, which progressively reduces the number of masked positions to refine image details. For extreme acceleration tests (Section <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Experiments in Extremely Low-Step Generation Scenarios ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>), we utilize a 5-step linear schedule to evaluate the sampler’s robustness under severe budget constraints.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Creative Writing.</span> We evaluate creative writing performance using 200 prompts selected from the Alpaca dataset. Following the Min-P paper <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nguyen et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, we employ GPT-4.1 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">OpenAI, 2025</a>)</cite> as an LLM judge to assess generation quality. For this experiment, the maximum generation length is set to 1024 tokens, with a fixed block size of 16.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Theoretical Analysis of the Info-Gain Objective</h2>

<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Setup and notation.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At decoding step <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the current state and <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> the set of masked positions.
For each <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell\in\mathcal{M}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell\in\mathcal{M}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, define the per-position predictive entropy</p>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For an action <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> selecting positions <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}\subseteq\mathcal{M}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>⊆</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}\subseteq\mathcal{M}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, the next state is <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t-1}=\mathrm{Apply}(z_{t},a_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Apply</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t-1}=\mathrm{Apply}(z_{t},a_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{t-1}=\mathcal{M}_{t}\setminus A_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∖</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{t-1}=\mathcal{M}_{t}\setminus A_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. The Info-Gain objective is defined as</p>

</section>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Expected information gain.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Sampling <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> from a sampler <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\pi(\cdot\mid z_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(\cdot\mid z_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> induces randomness in <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{IG}(a_{t};z_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>IG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{IG}(a_{t};z_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{\mathrm{IG}}(a_{t};z_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mi>IG</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{\mathrm{IG}}(a_{t};z_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>. Let</p>
<table id="A3.E17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

</table>
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where the expectation is over the sampled token assignments while keeping <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> fixed.</p>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="59.69" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 477.38 59.69" width="477.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,59.69) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#4040FF;" fill="#4040FF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 4.15 L 0 55.53 C 0 57.83 1.86 59.69 4.15 59.69 L 473.23 59.69 C 475.52 59.69 477.38 57.83 477.38 55.53 L 477.38 4.15 C 477.38 1.86 475.52 0 473.23 0 L 4.15 0 C 1.86 0 0 1.86 0 4.15 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#F2F2FF;" fill="#F2F2FF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.38 4.15 L 1.38 55.53 C 1.38 57.06 2.62 58.3 4.15 58.3 L 473.23 58.3 C 474.75 58.3 475.99 57.06 475.99 55.53 L 475.99 4.15 C 475.99 2.62 474.75 1.38 473.23 1.38 L 4.15 1.38 C 2.62 1.38 1.38 2.62 1.38 4.15 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 13.62 43.37)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:32.53em;--ltx-fo-height:0.69em;--ltx-fo-depth:2.65em;font-size:10pt;" height="46.28" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.61)" width="450.12"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:32.53em;">
<span id="A3.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition C.1</span></span><span id="A3.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Upper bound on expected information gain)<span id="A3.Thmtheorem1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<span id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">For any state <math id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">z</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and position set <math id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}\subseteq\mathcal{M}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">A</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">⊆</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathcolor="#000000">ℳ</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}\subseteq\mathcal{M}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></span>
<span id="A3.E18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<span><span class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></span>
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{I}(A_{t};z_{t})\leq C(a_{t}\mid z_{t}),\qquad\text{and thus}\quad J_{MI}(A_{t};z_{t})\geq 0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" J_{MI}(A_{t};z_{t})\geq 0.</annotation></semantics></math></span>

<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">Define</span></p>

<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">Then <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C(a_{t}\mid z_{t})=|A_{t}|\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C(a_{t}\mid z_{t})=|A_{t}|\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}(z_{t})=\gamma\alpha+(1-\gamma)\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}(z_{t})=\gamma\alpha+(1-\gamma)\beta</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y:=X^{(A_{t})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>:=</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y:=X^{(A_{t})}</annotation></semantics></math> be the sampled assignments. For any <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell\in\mathcal{M}_{t-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell\in\mathcal{M}_{t-1}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>

<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text">By the entropy-reduction decomposition,</span></p>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Case 1:</span> <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha\leq\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha\leq\beta</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(Y;X^{(\ell)}\mid z_{t})\leq|A_{t}|\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>;</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;X^{(\ell)}\mid z_{t})\leq|A_{t}|\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>, giving</p>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Case 2:</span> <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha&gt;\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha&gt;\beta</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(Y;X^{(\ell)}\mid z_{t})\leq H^{(\ell)}(z_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>;</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;X^{(\ell)}\mid z_{t})\leq H^{(\ell)}(z_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> and</p>
<table id="A3.E23" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{I}(A_{t};z_{t})\leq\gamma(\alpha-\beta)+\beta\leq\alpha\leq|A_{t}|\alpha=C(a_{t}\mid z_{t})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>I</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>≤</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{I}(A_{t};z_{t})\leq\gamma(\alpha-\beta)+\beta\leq\alpha\leq|A_{t}|\alpha=C(a_{t}\mid z_{t}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(23)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text">In both cases, <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{I}(A_{t};z_{t})\leq C(a_{t}\mid z_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>I</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{I}(A_{t};z_{t})\leq C(a_{t}\mid z_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>, implying</span></p>
<table id="A3.E24" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E24.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{MI}(A_{t};z_{t})=C(a_{t}\mid z_{t})-\tilde{I}(A_{t};z_{t})\geq 0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>I</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{MI}(A_{t};z_{t})=C(a_{t}\mid z_{t})-\tilde{I}(A_{t};z_{t})\geq 0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(24)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p7.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p7.2.1" class="ltx_text">∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Practical implications.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Proposition <a href="#A3.Thmtheorem1" title="Proposition C.1 (Upper bound on expected information gain). ‣ Expected information gain. ‣ Appendix C Theoretical Analysis of the Info-Gain Objective ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.1</span></a> establishes that, for any fixed position set <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, the expected Info-Gain objective <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{MI}(A_{t};z_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{MI}(A_{t};z_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> is non-negative. This provides a theoretical guarantee that, on average, the cost of committing to selected positions is never underestimated relative to the actual reduction in state uncertainty. In practice, we find that the realized <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{\mathrm{IG}}(a_{t};z_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mi>IG</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{\mathrm{IG}}(a_{t};z_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>, computed along individual decoding trajectories, closely tracks this expectation. On benchmarks such as GSM8K, more than <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%</annotation></semantics></math> of observed <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{\mathrm{IG}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>J</mi><mi>IG</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{\mathrm{IG}}</annotation></semantics></math> values are non-negative or slightly below zero (e.g., <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="J_{\mathrm{IG}}\geq-5\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>IG</mi></msub><mo rspace="0em">≥</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{\mathrm{IG}}\geq-5\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>), indicating that the bound is rarely violated.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Furthermore, <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{IG}(a_{t};z_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>IG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{IG}(a_{t};z_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> is highly semantically sensitive: it captures not only the immediate uncertainty of the chosen positions but also how these assignments influence the uncertainty of the remaining masked positions. As a result, <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{\mathrm{IG}}(a_{t};z_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mi>IG</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{\mathrm{IG}}(a_{t};z_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> naturally discourages actions that would commit to poorly conditioned or inconsistent states, effectively preventing error propagation during decoding. This behavior manifests as a strong implicit correction mechanism, enabling the sampler to recover from suboptimal early decisions and maintain coherent, high-quality generation. Overall, the Info-Gain objective provides a computationally efficient and robust signal for action selection, balancing immediate certainty with long-term state stability throughout the iterative decoding process.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18176v1/bound.png" id="A3.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:238/239;" width="238" height="239" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A3.F6.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="A3.F6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Empirical distribution of <math id="A3.F6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{IG}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>J</mi><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{IG}</annotation></semantics></math> values sorted from highest to lowest. The 5th percentile is <math id="A3.F6.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="-5\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-5\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>, indicating the bound is rarely violated in practice.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>

<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Experiments in Extremely Low-Step Generation Scenarios</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we present additional experimental results for scenarios where the number of decoding steps is severely constrained.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">First, we present the results for the ImageNet-512 benchmark using the MMaDa model in a text-to-image generation setting. The experimental configuration is similar to that in Section <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>, with the key difference being the use of a linear step schedule and a highly constrained budget of only 5 decoding steps. As shown in Figure <a href="#A5.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ Appendix E Experiments in Extremely Low-Step Generation Scenarios ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>, our method demonstrates significantly better visual quality and structural coherence under these extreme conditions. Furthermore, we visualize the evolution of cumulative entropy averaged over 10,000 sampled instances in Figure <a href="#A5.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Appendix E Experiments in Extremely Low-Step Generation Scenarios ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.F7" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="A5.F7.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2602.18176v1/IGS.png" id="A5.F7.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/238;" width="476" height="238" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F7.sf1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(a)</span> </span><span id="A5.F7.sf1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Info-Gain</span></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="A5.F7.sf2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2602.18176v1/Confidence.png" id="A5.F7.sf2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/238;" width="476" height="238" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F7.sf2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(b)</span> </span><span id="A5.F7.sf2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Confidence</span></figcaption>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F7.sf3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(c)</span> </span><span id="A5.F7.sf3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Entropy</span></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="A5.F7.sf4" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2602.18176v1/margin.png" id="A5.F7.sf4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/238;" width="476" height="238" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F7.sf4.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(d)</span> </span><span id="A5.F7.sf4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Margin</span></figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>: </span><span id="A5.F7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Visual results on ImageNet-512 with an extreme budget of only 5 decoding steps. The Info-Gain Sampler maintains superior structural coherence compared to baseline heuristics.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A5.F8" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18176v1/imagenet256-compare.png" id="A5.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:238/238;" width="238" height="238" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F8.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 8</span>: </span><span id="A5.F8.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Evolution of cumulative entropy during image generation on the Image256 benchmark. The results are averaged over all labels using a 5-step linear schedule. The curves illustrate how Info-Gain Sampler manages global uncertainty compared to other methods throughout the decoding process.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To further evaluate the robustness of our sampler, we conduct an ultra-low step generation experiment using the Dream Model. We construct a simple writing task containing 50 prompts (e.g., “Write a story about a cat”) and require the model to decode the content within a very small number of steps, for a fixed length of 80 tokens. In this extreme regime, most baselines fail to generate meaningful and coherent text. We record the ”Collapse Step” for each method, defined as the minimum number of steps required to ensure that fewer than 50% of the generated samples exhibit severe repetitions or grammatical errors.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p4.1" class="ltx_p">For all experiments, the token sampling temperature is set to 0.4. For Info-Gain Sampler, the position sampling temperature is 0.4 and the number of action sets is <math id="A5.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=8</annotation></semantics></math>. The results are summarized in Table <a href="#A5.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ Appendix E Experiments in Extremely Low-Step Generation Scenarios ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.T7" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A5.T7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 7</span>: </span><span id="A5.T7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Comparison of Collapse Steps on ultra-low step writing tasks. Lower values indicate better robustness in extreme acceleration scenarios.</span></figcaption>
<table id="A5.T7.5" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_align_middle">
<tr id="A5.T7.5.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A5.T7.5.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt">Sampler</td>
<td id="A5.T7.5.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt">Collapse Step (<math id="A5.T7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>)</td></tr>
<tr id="A5.T7.5.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A5.T7.5.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t">Entropy</td>
<td id="A5.T7.5.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t">13</td></tr>
<tr id="A5.T7.5.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A5.T7.5.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left">Confidence</td>
<td id="A5.T7.5.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">12</td></tr>
<tr id="A5.T7.5.4" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A5.T7.5.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left">Margin</td>
<td id="A5.T7.5.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">12</td></tr>
<tr id="A5.T7.5.5" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A5.T7.5.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb"><span id="A5.T7.5.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Info-Gain</span></td>
<td id="A5.T7.5.5.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A5.T7.5.5.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">8</span></td></tr>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="A5.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The purpose of both experiments in ultra-low step generation is to evaluate how to generate meaningful content under conditions of extremely limited information and few decoding steps. The performance of the greedy sampler is significantly inferior to that of the Info-Gain Sampler. This demonstrates that by balancing the utilization of immediate information with the information gain for future decisions, the Info-Gain Sampler effectively achieves the most meaningful generation within a restricted number of decoding steps.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Resource Overhead Analysis</h2>

<section id="A6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.1 </span>Memory Overhead Analysis</h3>

<div id="A6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{W}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>W</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{W}</annotation></semantics></math> denote model weights, <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{A}</annotation></semantics></math> activations, and <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{C}(L)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{C}(L)</annotation></semantics></math> the KV-cache for sequence length <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math>. The key difference lies in how memory scales with the number of candidates <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="A6.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A6.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Non-cached Inference:</span> <math id="A6.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{\text{total}}=M_{W}+N\cdot M_{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mtext>total</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>W</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{\text{total}}=M_{W}+N\cdot M_{A}</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Info-Gain Sampler (Shared Prefix):</span> <math id="A6.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{\text{total}}=M_{W}+M_{C}(L-1)+N\cdot M_{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mtext>total</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>W</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{\text{total}}=M_{W}+M_{C}(L-1)+N\cdot M_{A}</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Info-Gain Beam Search (Diverse Prefixes):</span> <math id="A6.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{\text{total}}=M_{W}+N\cdot M_{C}(L-1)+N\cdot M_{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mtext>total</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>W</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>C</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{\text{total}}=M_{W}+N\cdot M_{C}(L-1)+N\cdot M_{A}</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For Info-Gain Sampler, the additional memory cost for increasing <math id="A6.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> is dominated by transient activations <math id="A6.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{A}</annotation></semantics></math>, which are relatively small compared to weights <math id="A6.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{W}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>W</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{W}</annotation></semantics></math>. In contrast, Info-Gain Beam Search requires storing <math id="A6.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> separate KV-caches <math id="A6.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{C}(L-1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{C}(L-1)</annotation></semantics></math>, leading to linear memory explosion with <math id="A6.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>. This is shown in Table <a href="#A6.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ F.1 Memory Overhead Analysis ‣ Appendix F Resource Overhead Analysis ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a></p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.T8" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A6.T8.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 8</span>: </span><span id="A6.T8.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Memory efficiency comparison under KV-caching.</span></figcaption>
<div id="A6.T8.5" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_center ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:345.0pt;height:35.1pt;vertical-align:-15.2pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(-10.2pt,1.0pt) scale(0.94441759094051,0.94441759094051) ;">
<table id="A6.T8.5.1" class="ltx_tabular ltx_align_middle">
<tr id="A6.T8.5.1.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.T8.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt"><span id="A6.T8.5.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Method</span></td>
<td id="A6.T8.5.1.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="A6.T8.5.1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">KV-Cache Count</span></td>
<td id="A6.T8.5.1.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="A6.T8.5.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Memory Scaling</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.T8.5.1.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.T8.5.1.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t">Info-Gain Sampler</td>
<td id="A6.T8.5.1.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t">1 (shared)</td>
<td id="A6.T8.5.1.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><math id="A6.T8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(M_{W}+M_{C}+N\cdot M_{A})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>W</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(M_{W}+M_{C}+N\cdot M_{A})</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.T8.5.1.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.T8.5.1.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb">Info-Gain Beam Search</td>
<td id="A6.T8.5.1.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><math id="A6.T8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> (diverse)</td>
<td id="A6.T8.5.1.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><math id="A6.T8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(M_{W}+B\cdot M_{C}+N\cdot B\cdot M_{A})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>W</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>C</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(M_{W}+B\cdot M_{C}+N\cdot B\cdot M_{A})</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="A6.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Empirical measurements on TraDo-8B-Instruct (512 tokens, block size 16) validate this analysis. As shown in Figure <a href="#A6.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ F.2 Computation Overhead Analysis ‣ Appendix F Resource Overhead Analysis ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>, Info-Gain Sampler maintains stable memory usage with only 24% overhead at <math id="A6.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=8</annotation></semantics></math>, while Info-Gain Beam Search exhibits substantial memory surge due to divergent trajectory caching.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.2 </span>Computation Overhead Analysis</h3>

<div id="A6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The computational overhead of Info-Gain Sampler stems primarily from evaluating <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> candidates per step. The theoretical time complexity is:</p>
<table id="A6.E25" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E25.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\text{theoretical}}=K\cdot N\cdot T_{f}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext>theoretical</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>f</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\text{theoretical}}=K\cdot N\cdot T_{f}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(25)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> is decoding steps, <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> is candidates per step, and <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{f}</annotation></semantics></math> is one forward pass cost.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Practical optimizations significantly reduce overhead:</span></p>
<ol id="A6.I2" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A6.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A6.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Batched Parallel Evaluation:</span> All <math id="A6.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> candidates are processed simultaneously:</p>
<table id="A6.E26" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E26.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\text{batch}}=K\cdot(T_{f}+\epsilon),\quad\epsilon\ll(N-1)T_{f}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext>batch</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>≪</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>f</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\text{batch}}=K\cdot(T_{f}+\epsilon),\quad\epsilon\ll(N-1)T_{f}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(26)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A6.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">KV-Cache Reuse:</span> Shared prefix reduces attention computation:</p>
<table id="A6.E27" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E27.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\text{cached}}\approx K\cdot T_{\text{prefix}}+\frac{K(N-1)}{N}T_{\text{attn}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext>cached</mtext></msub><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext>prefix</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext>attn</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\text{cached}}\approx K\cdot T_{\text{prefix}}+\frac{K(N-1)}{N}T_{\text{attn}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(27)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A6.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">High-confidence Bypass:</span> If the maximum token probability exceeds a threshold <math id="A6.I2.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>, the full sampling routine is skipped to reduce latency.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in Fig. <a href="#A6.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ F.2 Computation Overhead Analysis ‣ Appendix F Resource Overhead Analysis ‣ Improving Sampling for Masked Diffusion Models via Information Gain" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>, our adaptive threshold mechanism effectively manages computational cost while maintaining high decoding quality. By dynamically adjusting the candidate acceptance threshold, we achieve near-optimal entropy reduction with minimal time overhead. This explains why practical speedups (1.2–1.5<math id="A6.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>) are significantly better than theoretical predictions (<math id="A6.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="N\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\times</annotation></semantics></math>). While evaluating more candidates (<math id="A6.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>) increases per-step cost, it often reduces total steps (<math id="A6.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>) needed for convergence. Our batched implementation and threshold optimization ensure that the quality improvements are achieved with only a modest increase in overhead (typically 20–40% on average for reasoning tasks).</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F9" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18176v1/abla-3.png" id="A6.F9.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/165;" width="429" height="165" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A6.F9.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 9</span>: </span><span id="A6.F9.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Effect of utility threshold on cumulative entropy reduction and generation time. </span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A6.F10" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18176v1/gpu-compare.png" id="A6.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:381/190;" width="381" height="190" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A6.F10.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 10</span>: </span><span id="A6.F10.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Memory usage comparison. Info-Gain Sampler maintains low overhead via prefix sharing.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>

    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
  </div>
